title: Material Type
content: **** Express the fabric in various material types! **** 1. Click the Object Browser ▶ Fabric Property Editor ▶ Material ▶ **Type**. 2. Refer to the table below to adjust fabric gloss and hardware material. **Name** | **Description** ---|--- **Type** | Choose the reflection type to express fabric gloss more realistically as needed. **Fabric_Matte** | Reflection is adjusted optimal to express general fabric. **Fabric_Shiny** | Reflection is adjusted optimal to express shiny fabric. **Fabric_Silk/Satin** | Reflection is adjusted optimal to express silk or satin fabric. **Fabric_Velvet** | Reflection is adjusted optimal to express velvet fabric. [**Denim**](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/48703338325145-Express-Denim-Wet-Wash) | ![Label.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/48709108912665) Express Denim wet wash effects. [**Fur_(Render Only)**](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360001526568) | Express realistic fur. **Gem (Render Only)** | Express gem material. Gem material is similar with glass, but expresses light reflection in multiple color. Adjust the opacity with the **Absorption** value. Lower the value is, more transparent the object is. The **Absorption** value is relative to the object's thickness. Thicker the object is, lower the **Absorption** value should be. Adjust the **Abbe** value to increase or reduce light reflection effect. **Glass** | Reflection is adjusted optimal to express glass materials. Adjust the opacity with the **Absorption** value. Lower the value is, more transparent the object is. The **Absorption** value is relative to the object's thickness. Thicker the object is, lower the **Absorption** value should be. [**Glitter (Render Only)**](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360011005813) | Express glitter. **Light (Render Only)** | Use garments or objects as lights. Adjust the brightness with the **Color Mult** option. Higher the value is, brighter the light is. As the light gets brighter, the color of the light deviates from the one set by the user. **Leather** | Reflection is adjusted optimal to express leathers. **Metal** | Reflection is adjusted optimal to express metallic materials. **Plastic** | Reflection is adjusted optimal to express plastics. **Skin (Render Only)** | Render human skin more realistically. Light enters an object and scatters beneath its surface. Not all light reflects from a surface. The objects penetrating lights such as leaves, fruits, or candles also be used for this. **📝Note:** When using Skin, you should not use a displacement map since the compatibility issue with V-Ray. **Roughness** | **Intensity** | Edit fabric gloss by adjusting **Intensity** of the**Roughness**. **📝Note:** Since**** version **2024.0** , the Roughness Intensity ranges have been expanded. When loading legacy files, the displayed value is automatically converted (e.g., 50 becomes 100) to maintain the same visual appearance and compatibility. **Map** | Edit fabric gloss by adding and modifying **Roughness Map**. **Map** | Select the **Browse** button next to the **Map** option to add a **Roughness Map** to the selected Fabric style. **Map Intensity** | Adjust the Map's **Intensity**. **📝Note:** Since**** version **2024.0** , the Roughness Intensity ranges have been expanded. When loading legacy files, the displayed value is automatically converted (e.g., 50 becomes 100) to maintain the same visual appearance and compatibility. **Invert** | Select to invert the gloss of the fabric. When this option is selected, shinny part becomes dull and vice-versa. To use Specular Maps provided in CLO below ver4.0.0, check this option. **Reflection Intensity** | Greater the **Reflection Intensity** value is, more reflective the material or fabric is and vice-versa.
content_description: Explore and customize various fabric types and their properties to achieve realistic material reflections and textures.

title: Troubleshooting: Vray Render Problems
content: This article describes the causes and solutions to various problems that may occur during V-ray rendering in CLO software. If your CLO rendering is not working, freezing or extremely slow, please take a closer look at this article. And please note that this article does not describe everything related to rendering, but rather describes the main causes of problems and how to mitigate them. ![Lady_in_Hanbok_png.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44490647923481) <The image above is an example of a traditional woman dress rendered using V-ray in CLO software.> ## **Technical background** CLO software includes the [V-Ray Render SDK from Chaos](https://www.chaos.com/vray), allowing users to create photorealistic renders of their projects, including clothing and avatars. CLO's V-ray renderer supports both Windows and macOS, and can complete rendering faster via GPU acceleration, especially on Windows PCs equipped with Nvidia graphics cards. On Windows PCs and Macs without an Nvidia graphics card, rendering will be done via the CPU, and the results of CPU-based and GPU-based rendering will be almost identical. And one good news, starting with CLO v2025.0, GPU acceleration is available for V-ray rendering on Apple Silicon Macs. In the Render Engine list, you can choose GPU (Metal) in addition to CPU. Also note that acceleration performance via GPU (Metal) depends on the specifications of the GPU cores built into the Apple Silicon Mac and the CLO garment file and its properties. ## **Render Properties** ![004_render_properties.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44375524368025) ### Render Engine * **CPU** : This is the default render engine for CLO and will be locked to this engine on Windows PCs and Macs without Nvidia graphics cards. * **GPU (CUDA)** : This is an option for Windows PCs with Nvidia graphics cards. If you have a modern, high-performance Nvidia GPU, you can complete rendering about 2 to 6 times faster than CPU-based rendering. When rendering very light clothing, like a basic CLO t-shirt, there isn't much difference between GPU and CPU render times. GPU rendering is an option to choose when you want to process very complex and heavy garments quickly, and to do so, you need the latest high-performance Nvidia GPUs. * **CPU Supporting** : This feature adds idle CPU resources during GPU rendering to help render faster and smoother. We recommend leaving this option turned on. * **Low GPU Priority** : This will lower the GPU resources consumed during GPU rendering. You can turn this option on if you want to do other image/video work while rendering, but for fast and stable rendering, you may want to leave it off. ### Finish Conditions * Finish Conditions are literally options that determine how the render will be finished. * **Noise Threshold** : This determines how much noise will be suppressed in the rendered result image. The lower this value is, the better the rendered image quality is. However, as more calculations are performed, computing resources and rendering time increase dramatically. **Even with the default value of 0.05, sufficient quality rendering results can be obtained.** If you want to obtain better quality rendered images, try rendering while lowering this value step by step, like 0.05 > 0.04 > 0.03, and check the final quality. At the lowest values ​​near 0.001, it will take a long time to complete the render even on a high-performance computer. * **Max Render Time (min)** : This is a kind of timer, and when the time set here is elapsed, the render engine will stop even if the rendering has not completed yet. Lowering this value will not make rendering complete any faster. So if you set this value too low, you may see a rough rendered image result because it will stop in an unfinished rendering state. **It is actually better to set it to the maximum value of 100 minutes.** ## **Image/Video Properties** ![003_render_image_properties.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44374636184729) ### Image Size * As the image size increases, the amount of pixels the renderer has to process (i.e. the amount of computation) increases, which in turn increases the usage of the CPU, GPU, video memory, main memory, and the time to complete. If you want to render very large image sizes, make sure your computer is powerful enough to handle it, especially with plenty of memory. Most rendering scenarios can be handled well on a PC with around 32GB of memory and/or around 16GB of video memory, but scenarios such as super large image sizes or animation rendering may run into memory shortage issues. * If you need to continuously process sequential image scenes, such as turntable rendering, animation rendering, and colorway rendering, the load on your hardware and memory usage can increase significantly. Even in rendering scenarios that process sequential scenes like this, keep a close eye on memory usage. ## **Interactive Render vs. Final Render** * Interactive Render is a function that instantly renders changes to the scene that occur when you rotate or scale a garment in the 3D window, showing them within the Render window. That is, since it is a mode for fast and instantaneous rendering results, the image quality and details are reduced compared to Final Render. * Final Render is a function that renders based on the current garment and given render settings and saves the result as an image file or video. Even after Final Render is completed, you need to check the result saved as a file, not the result shown in the render window, to confirm the exact rendered result. Additionally, slight differences in image quality, color, and color tone may occur depending on the image/video viewer program. ## **Problem situations and how to solve them** * **"My computer has an Nvidia graphics card but GPU rendering is not enabled"** : This is either because the GPU device is disabled in Windows, the graphics card and monitor are not properly connected, or because of a graphics card driver error. Please check [this web post](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000296768-Graphics-Card-Problems-and-Troubleshooting) for solutions. * **"Can't render with Intel Graphics or AMD GPU?"** : CLO software supports both CPU and GPU rendering, with GPU rendering only available on PCs with Nvidia graphics cards and Apple Silicon Macs. Windows PCs with AMD or Intel graphics cards, and older Intel-chip-based Macs, only support CPU rendering. * **"So slow, rendering has been taking hours"** : Depending on how complex and heavy your project is, your computer's specifications, and the Render Finish Conditions described above, the render completion time will vary. Try rendering again after loosening the details and properties of the garment itself, as well as the render properties. * **"Freezing or crash happens while rendering"** : As above, it is a result of the complexity of the project, computer specifications, and rendering properties. Sometimes, crashes or rendering failures may occur due to graphics card driver errors, in which case, try updating to the latest graphics card drivers. * **"It shows out of video memory error"** : This occurs when there is not enough video memory to complete the rendering. Please readjust the render properties and image size, close all other programs using video memory, and then try rendering again. For example, starting Windows and opening just a web browser can take up about 600MB to 1GB of video memory. Under these conditions, if your graphics card has 8GB of video memory, your CLO will only be able to use about 7GB of video memory. So if you are running multiple programs in addition to the CLO software, it is recommended that you close them before rendering, as the CLO renderer may run out of video memory. * **"Rendering stops with an unknown error message"** : This is due to a setting error in Windows itself and/or a graphics card driver error. Update to the latest graphics card driver. * **"Garments containing fur and/or knitwear fabrics cannot be rendered, or it shows unexpected render results"** : Fur and knitwear rendering are among the most hardware-intensive of CLO's features. They require several to tens of times more calculations and use more memory than other clothing renderings. If your computer is struggling to handle this scenario, consider designing approaches that use images or textures to represent fur and knitwear. * **"GPU render results are slightly different from CPU render results"** : This is due to the nature of the V-Ray render SDK and may occur when rendering scenes with a large number of light sources and reflections, and very complex fabrics such as fur. This is a known issue for the CLO team and are continuously working on improving it. * **"V-Ray render cannot run because the required V-Ray library could not be loaded in the current environment"** : The CLO software is designed to load configuration files when starting vray-render. This error indicates that essential files for vray-render could not be loaded due to file permissions. The solution is to install the CLO software with administrator privileges, see [details here](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/17074279996697-Disk-access-rights-required-when-CLO-is-running#:~:text=to%20download%22%20appears.-,Windows,-1%C2%A0%20After%20logging). Security programs, such as antivirus programs, may restrict the execution of the CLO software or various files that comprise CLO. In the detailed settings of the installed or running security program, change both the execution of the CLO software and Internet connection to "Allow." ![008_vray_lib_load_fail.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/54219419608473) ## **How to check GPU and video memory usage** * You can check CPU, Memory, GPU, and GPU memory usage in the Performance tab of Windows Task Manager. Below, running just Windows and a web browser, you can see very low CPU and GPU usage, but you can see that the base memory usage is quite high. * When you run CLO to perform tasks like pattern editing, simulation, rendering, etc., you will see increased CPU, GPU, and memory usage. And it is normal for CPU and GPU usage to be close to 100% during simulation and rendering, and GPU usage will not stay at 100% during GPU-rendering. While GPU rendering, GPU usage continues to fluctuate because it is divided into sections where the GPU works, sections where the CPU works, and sections where they work simultaneously. ![007_GPU_usage.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44417445932569) The image above is what Windows Task Manager looks like during interactive-GPU-rendering. The Windows desktop PC specifications and project file details used for testing are as follows: * AMD Ryzen™ 9 7950X Processor (native 16-core), Nvidia RTX™ A6000 (vram 48GB), 64GB DDR5 memory, NVMe SSD 512GB, 4K resolution monitor, wired internet connection * Windows 11 Pro version 24H2 (OS Build 26100.3476), CLO v2024.2.328 * A traditional dress made of multiple layers, particle distance from 5 to 20, no trim, made with 55 patterns and 1144 sewing lines. Check out the links below for file download and tutorial. * CONNECT store: <https://connect.clo-set.com/portfolio/99263/collection/collections?itemId=5af7734d050c4e31987061fbf697a3a9> * YouTube tutorial: <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=T_UbvoshTpA> **1) CPU** : shows CPU usage. It doesn't always use 100% during rendering and it fluctuates. **2) Memory** : this is the total amount of memory used by Windows, the web browser, and CLO rendering. Windows itself uses about 4GB of memory, and the web browser uses about the same amount. The CLO software uses about 5 to 6GB of memory to do this level of garment rendering. Memory usage will vary depending on OS, hardware configuration, active programs, CLO garment files, and properties. **3) GPU** : shows GPU name and current usage. If you have a laptop or desktop with both integrated graphics and a discrete graphics card, you will see more than one GPU listed. As with CPU usage, it is not always 100% and fluctuates. **4) Dedicated GPU Memory** : shows the total amount of video memory installed on the graphics card and the currently used amount. Windows itself typically uses about 600MB to 1GB of video memory, and web browsers and other programs with graphical UI use a similar amount of video memory. Rendering in CLO typically starts at around 3GB of video memory, and can even use 20GB or more for very complex, continuous image processing scenarios such as animation rendering. Mac users who want to check hardware resources while running CLO software can use the [Activity Monitor](https://support.apple.com/guide/activity-monitor/welcome/mac) app which built in macOS. ## **See also** * [CLO system requirements](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000307168-CLO-system-requirements-March-2025) * [Graphics Card Problems and Troubleshooting](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000296768-Graphics-Card-Problems-and-Troubleshooting) * [How to workaround errors caused by faulty GPU drivers](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/44142966593177-How-to-workaround-errors-caused-by-faulty-GPU-drivers-Last-modified-Mar-2025) * [How to speed up CLO](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/23390057463577-How-to-Speed-Up-CLO)
content_description: This webpage aims to provide users with insights into common V-ray rendering issues in CLO software and effective solutions to enhance rendering performance.

title: Keyframe Animation
content: ## **New in CLO 2025.0** Add Keyframe Set Animation Layer Animation Track Set Keyframe Timleline Supported Objects By setting animation keys on an object’s properties, you can interpolate between keyframes to express animation over time. Edit the avatar’s joints to apply dynamic animations, or control the wind properties tocreate effects where the wind values change over time. Use these methods to create various animation effects. ![Youtube Icon.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/49947169529881) [Watch Video](https://youtu.be/p2oEiVd6_ZM) #### **Add Keyframe** 1. Click Animation ▶ **Animation Editor** in the top menu. 2. Click the **Add Animation** button at the top left of the Animation Editor to view a list of objects that can have animations. 3. Select the target item to create an empty layer with no keyframes. 4. Expand the created layer, set the value of a property that can be keyed, and click the **![Insert Key.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53244832282137)Insert Key** button. _* This action works the same as clicking**Insert Key** in the Property Editor._ __ 5. Move the **Current Frame** , change the property value, and click **Insert Key** again to create another keyframe. 6. When you play the animation between the multiple keyframes, you can see the value change over time. #### **Animation Layer** 1. Right-clicking the created layer will display a context menu. 2. Layer have a hierarchical structure, and only the properties of an object that can be keyed are displayed as layers. 3. Layers can be deleted, and sub-property layers can be re-created using the **Add Layer** menu of the parent layer. 4. An animation list item is structured as follows: **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Active Button** | When the button is turned on, the keyframes in the layer become active and functional. Child layers are dependent on the active status of their parent layer. **Layer Name** | The top-level layer displays its name along with an icon. Property layers display only the name. The layer name is synchronized with the actual target’s name. **Parameter Value** | Shows the value of the corresponding property and allows you to edit it. This value is synchronized with the Property Editor and will update together. **Key Controller** | Enables the insertion of keyframes and provides navigation to the previous or next keyframe. **📝Note:** Recorded **Cache Layer** only can be cut or merged. #### **Animation Track** 1. **Top Level Object Layer** * The object layer displays the Start-End keyframe range as a bar. * Hover the mouse over the bar to display the handles and precisely adjust its length. * As the length of the bar changes, the keyframes in the child layers stretch or shrink while maintaining their relative spacing. 2. **Property Layer** * Actual keyframes are set on property layers. * Property layers can also be grouped, and the parent key in the group represents the keys of its children. * When the parent key is selected, all child keys on the same frame are selected as well, and actions such as moving, copying, deleting, or changing interpolation type are applied collectively. #### **Set Keyframe** 1. **Manual Keyframe Creation** * Change the property value of the target object in the Animation Layer or Property Editor, then click the **Intert Keyframe** button. * The current property value of the target object will be set as a key at the current frame. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/49947670722969)** 2. **Automatic Keyframe Creation** * Enable **Auto Keying**. * Manually set the first key using the manual creation method. * After the initial key is set, any changes to the same property will automatically create a key at the current frame. **📝Note:** The first key must be manually set in order for subsequent keys to be created automatically on that property. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/49947670722969)** ![20252.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/51957439965465) 3. **Create Keyframes or Layers in Batch** * When ![Add Keyframe for Selected Layers.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53244816870809) **Add Keyframe for Selected Layers** is executed from the **Animation Toolbar** , keyframes are created for all currently selected layers. * When ![Add Keyframe for All Layers.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53244816877337) **Add Keyframe for All Layers** is executed from the **Animation Toolbar** , keyframes are created for all layers. * When ![Create All Object Layers.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53244816880281) **Create All Object Layers** is executed from the **Animation Toolbar** , layers are created for all scene objects existing in the current world. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/49947670722969)** 4. **Copy and Paste Keyframes** * One or more keyframes can be copied and pasted relative to the current frame. * Meaningful paste results can only be achieved when pasting onto layers with the same data type. * When multiple keys are pasted, they retain the same spacing relative to the current frame. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/49947670722969)** 5. **Keyframe Interpolation Types** * To set the interpolation type, select keys and right-click to open the context menu. Choose the desired interpolation type from the menu. * Keyframe interpolation types can be set as follows: **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Linear** | Creates a straight-line interpolation between keys, producing a constant rate of change. **Cubic** | Creates a curved interpolation between keys, resulting in dynamic changes. This is visible when three or more keys are present. **Constant** | Maintains the current key's value until just before the next key. * To apply the same interpolation type to all child keys, select the parent key of the property and change its interpolation type. All child keys will be updated accordingly. #### **Timeline** **Playback Range Context Menu** 1. Use the following features to easily set the playback range. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Set Start Frame** | Sets the current frame as the start frame of the playback range. This menu is disabled if the current frame is larger than the end frame. **Set End Frame** | Sets the current frame as the end frame of the playback range. This menu is disabled if the current frame is less than the start frame. **Clamp Range to Active Frames** | Automatically adjusts the playback range to fit the span between the first and last keyframes across all layers. _**✨Tip:** _Quickly adjust the animation playback range based on specific layers. [![Youtube Icon.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/49947169529881) Watch Video](https://youtu.be/WIQVkxGPmB4?si=tJ_6-OMdOkfWcnK_) Use **Clamp Range to Selected Layers** from the track context menu of an animation layer to adjust the playback range. The range will automatically match the start and end keyframes of the selected layers. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/49947670722969)** **Slider Context Menu** 1. Right-click the slider at the bottom of the Timeline and use the following options to control the Timeline view area. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Fit to Active Frames** | Adjusts the Timeline View to fit the Start Keyframe and End Keyframe. **Fit to Playback Range** | Adjusts the Timeline View to fit the Playback Range's Start Frame and End Frame. **Fit to Full Frames** | Adjusts the Timeline View to fir the defined Minimum Frame and Maximum Frame. #### **Supported Objects** Keyframe animation can be applied to the following objects: **Object** | **Description** ---|--- **Colorway** | The following properties can be controlled: \- Colorways **📝Note:** Keyframe can be inserted by clicking the **Insert Key** button located at the top right of the Colorway Editor. **Fabric** | The following properties can be controlled: * Front/Back/Side Material * Physical Property **📝Note:** If **Use Same Material as Front** is enabled for the back/side material, it will not appear in the Layer. **Pattern** | The following properties can be controlled: * Fabric Index * Solidify * Shrinkage Weft/ Warp (%) * Pressure **📝Note:** It is possible to transition between fabrics assigned to a pattern. When switching fabrics, the property values are interpolated. **Avatar** | The following properties can be controlled: * Joint **Trim** | The following properties can be controlled: * Weight (g) **Camera** | The following properties can be controlled: * Transform * Local Camera Position * Aim Position * Field of View **Pin** | The following properties can be controlled: * Activate **Tack** | The following properties can be controlled: * Activate * Thread Length (mm) **Wind Controller** | The following properties can be controlled: * Active * Unlimited Bound * Transform * Strength * Decay * Frequency * Turbulence **Simulation Property** | The following properties can be controlled: * Gravity * Air Damping **Cache** | Recorded Cache is classified into the following two types. * Garment Cache Caches recorded during simulation are keyed and categorized into Pattern and Trim Layers. * Softbody Cache Avatar motion recorded after enabling Softbody. **📝Note:** Cache layers can be cut and merged individually by type. **Render Light** | Apply keyframes to [render lights](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115014899168-Edit-V-Ray-Light-Properties). **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/49947670722969)** * **Rectangle Light** \- Activate \- Intensity \- Color \- Width \- Height * **Sphere Light** \- Activate \- Intensity \- Color \- Radius * **Directional Light** \- Activate \- Intensity \- Color * **Spot Light** \- Activate \- Intensity \- Color \- Cone Angle \- Penumbra Angle \- Shadow Radius * **IES Light** \- Activate \- Color \- If Intensity is set to Custom: Intensity Value * **Dome Light** \- Activate \- Light Intensity \- Light Angle _If Finite Dome is activated: Even when switched to Off while a key is set as On, the animation layer will not be visible, but the key value will be retained._ \- Radius \- Projection Height \- Ground Blend
content_description: Explore the new animation features in CLO 2025.0, including keyframe set creation, layer management, and object support, to enhance your animation projects with dynamic effects and seamless property transitions.

title: How can I get a trial version of CLO?
content: **Question** How can I get a trial version of CLO? **Answer** CLO offers a CLO free trial for 14 days, and all users eligible for an Individual license can use a one-time free trial. *Your paid subscription will automatically start right after the trial expires and you can cancel your trial before renewal, avoiding charges. **Important Note:** To receive the student discount, you must verify your student status before starting your trial. If you fail to do so, you will not be eligible for the discount. [Does CLO offer student discounts?](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115013366988-Does-CLO-offer-student-discounts) **Eligibility for a CLO free trial** CLO Trial License can be started via the subscription button on the CLO web and is strictly reserved for a hobbyist, freelancer, self-employed individual, or one person-company who qualifies for an Individual License according to our [Terms of Service](https://legal.clo-set.com/additional-clo) (2.2.1). *Enterprise and Academic entities must contact CLO Business Development Team via Contact Us separately to obtain the appropriate Trial License. **Start your CLO free trial** You must sign up first if you don't have a CLO account yet. 1. title: Can I use my license on multiple devices?
content: **Question** Can I use my license on multiple devices? **Answer** Yes, you can install and use CLO on another computer. However, you cannot access CLO on multiple computers at the same time. To use CLO on a new computer, you must first log out of the software on your current one. If you are unable to log out (for example, due to an unexpected shutdown), you will need to manually remove your device. Please refer to the following article for instructions: [Remove Device from CLO website](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/1500000942261-Remove-Device-from-CLO-website) For [CLO for Enterprise](https://www.clo3d.com/enterprise), please reach out to CLO via [Contact Us](https://www.clo3d.com/support/contactus). *CLO software provides only on Windows/ macOS, not on mobile or iPad. Please refer to the [CLO System Requirements](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000307168-CLO-system-requirements-June-2021-) for more information on the device specification.
content_description: This webpage provides essential information about using your CLO license across multiple devices, including instructions for logging out and managing device access.

title: I get the pop-up about the suspension of Individual plan. What should I do?
content: **Question** I get the pop-up about the suspension of Individual plan. What should I do? I can see the watermark in the middle of the CLO screen. **Answer** If you see this pop-up and watermark on your CLO screen, this means you are potentially in violation of CLO license policy and are belonging to one of the following: * a member of an entity that has at least one(1) full-time employee other than you. * making purchases of our Services or CLO Software using a corporate credit card. * registering for a CLO account using a corporate email account, corporate email address, or corporate domain name. * accessing the CLO Software through a computer owned by an Enterprise/Academic entity. Please note that the eligibility of Individual plan is a one-person company, a sole proprietorship, a single-member LLC that does not elect to be treated as a corporation for tax purposes (“disregarded entity”), a freelancer, a self-employed independent contractor, or similarly situated self-employee otherwise in business for yourself. To remove the suspension for Individual subscription, you need to be verified through independent documentation such as articles of incorporation, business registration, tax returns/filings, proof of Self-Employment Tax payment, etc. Please [contact us](https://www.clo3d.com/contact) with your account and corresponsive documentation.
content_description: This web page provides guidance on resolving the suspension of your Individual plan due to potential violations of the CLO license policy.

title: Does CLO offer refunds?
content: **Question** Does CLO offer refunds? **Answer** Unfortunately, we do not offer refunds as stated within CLO's Terms of Service agreement. However, in limited cases, **a self-service refund is available within 24 hours of your first billing after a free trial**. You can find more details in this article: [Self-Service Refunds Within 24 Hours of First Billing After Free Trial](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/46600845755161-Self-Service-Refunds-Within-24-Hours-of-First-Billing-After-Free-Trial) Please note that CLO provides auto-renewal subscriptions for individual users, showing a clear notification on the checkout page and asking for your consent before you purchase CLO, as shown below. *Auto-renewal and cancellation policy * Your subscription will automatically renew each billing cycle (monthly or annually, depending on your plan) until canceled. Your selected payment method will be charged at the beginning of each billing period. * You may cancel at any time from your Subscription page to avoid future charges. Cancellations take effect at the end of the current billing cycle, and you will retain access to your account until that date. No refunds will be issued for the current billing cycle. * Upon cancellation, you will receive a confirmation email from CLO. If you do not receive a cancellation confirmation email within 24 hours, it is your responsibility to promptly contact CLO to obtain written confirmation. Without such confirmation, your cancellation request will be considered invalid. * Individual users are eligible for a refund within 24 hours of the first billing renewal following the free trial. Refunds can be approved automatically during this 24-hour window. If you receive a refund confirmation email without having requested a refund, or notice any suspicious activity, please contact us immediately. ---
content_description: This web page provides information on CLO's refund policy, including details about self-service refunds available within 24 hours of the first billing after a free trial and the auto-renewal subscription process.

title: Is it OK to use non-genuine CLO software?
content: **Question** Is it OK to use non-genuine CLO software? **Answer** CLO Virtual Fashion Inc. does not approve the supply or use of non-genuine CLO software, and it is not “OK.” Furthermore, spyware and viruses can be spread using non-genuine CLO software. According to IDC, firms that receive or install unauthorized software or purchase a computer with unlicensed software have a one-in-three probability of encountering malware (29 percent). To protect you against non-genuine CLO software, please purchase from [clo3d.com](https://www.clo3d.com/pricing) or [an authorized reseller](https://www.clo3d.com/business/partners) to ensure that you are getting authentic CLO software. CLO works hard to keep you safe from fraudulent sellers by ensuring that only genuine CLO software is available for purchase. ****If you are seeing this popup even after downloading the software from the official CLO website, please try the following methods.** ![20251202_110045.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/52945840727321) * Try closing CLO completely and then launching it again. * Wait for 15 minutes after closing CLO. Then, log into the CLO website and navigate to your user account page. If the 'Remove Device' button is active, click it and then try to launch CLO again. * If the methods above do not work, please try uninstalling and then reinstalling CLO. If none of these solutions resolve the issue, please [contact us](https://clo3d.com/en/support/contactus) for further assistance.
content_description: This webpage aims to inform users about the dangers of using non-genuine CLO software and provide guidance on ensuring the authenticity of their CLO purchases.

title: MetaHuman DNA Importer
content: **New in CLO 2025.2** [**MetaHuman**](https://www.metahuman.com/en-US) is a next-generation digital human creation technology introduced by Epic Games, offering ultra-realistic character modeling and rigging that are almost indistinguishable from reality. Based on high-resolution 3D scans of real people, it enables precise expression of facial features, skin textures, hair, and body proportions, and works seamlessly with **Unreal Engine** for use in virtual fittings, films, games, and more. Now, **CLO** allows direct import of **MetaHuman DNA data** , enabling garment creation that reflects realistic facial structures and body proportions with exceptional accuracy. **📝****Note:** DNA is the file format (*.dna) used for MetaHuman data. 1. Prepare the Body and Head files (*.dna) extracted from the MetaHuman Editor (Unreal Engine). 2. Go to **File → Import/Import (Add) → DNA** to open the **MetaHuman DNA Importer**. 3. Load both the Body and Head DNA files. 4. Set the import options as needed. **Options** | **Description** ---|--- **File** | **Body** | Load the Body file of the MetaHuman. **Head** | Load the Head file of the MetaHuman. **Basic** | **Unit** | Select the desired unit and enter the scale as a numerical value. **Options** | **Auto Add Arrangement Points** | For humanoid avatars only, arrangement points are automatically generated in the import process. **Auto Create Fitting Suit** | For humanoid avatars only, a Fitting Suit is automatically created in the import process. **Axis Conversion** | Modifying Object's Axis direction. 5. A seamless MetaHuman that combines the head and body will be imported as an avatar type. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/51882599850009)** **📝****Note:** * Enable **Avatar Display → Show Avatar Joint** to control the pose in your desired form. * Create animations by setting keyframes on the joints. * Applying motion files(*.mtn) is not supported.
content_description: Discover how CLO 2025.2 seamlessly integrates Epic Games' ultra-realistic MetaHuman technology for precise character modeling and garment creation, enabling lifelike virtual experiences.

title: Texture Editor
content: **List of Contents** Open Texture Editor Image Layer Canvas Settings Image Properties Preview Settings Apply Texture Save Texture Image Express complex graphics by overlaying multiple images. When images repeat, create seamless graphics by editing their outlines while referring to the preview. [![Youtube Icon.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44161782043801) Watch Tutorial Video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-baNp2a94_k) #### **Open Texture Editor** 1. In the Property Editor, click the ![More.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44161782045721) **More** icon at the far right next to a map, then click 'Open Texture Editor'. ![Fabric Properties.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44161809573017) #### **Image Layer** 1. Set the image layer in the list of layers at the bottom left of the Texture Editor. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Add** | Click the Add button to add the image as a new layer. Select and Import desired artboards and layers from AI/PDF files. **Copy** | Select the added layer and click the Copy button to copy it. **Lock** | Click the Lock button to lock the layer so that it is not edited. **Layer Order** | Click and drag the layer to change the order. **Show** | Click the Show(eye) icon to view or hide the layer on the window. **Delete** | Click the Delete button to delete the layer. **Rename** | Double-click the name of the layer to edit it and press enter to apply it. #### **Canvas Setting** 1. At the top of the texture editor, set up the canvas as needed. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Size** | Set the width and height of the canvas. Adjust the canvas size to the size of a specific image by right-clicking of the layer. **Unit** | Set the units of the canvas and image. **PPI (Pixels)** | Set the resolution of the canvas. **Transparent Background** | Set the image to a Transparent Background. #### **** **Image properties** 1. Set the Image properties of the selected layer in the Properties list at the bottom right of the Texture Editor. **Properties** | **Description** ---|--- **Paint** | **Blend** | Mix the selected layer with the bottom layer. [**Color**](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360047316974-Fabric-Color) | Set the color of the image. **Color Switch** | **Number** | Set the number of colors to extract from the image. **Sub Color** | Click the extracted color chip to change it to the different color. **Opacity** | Adjust the Opacity of the image. [**Desaturate**](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/ko/articles/115000471548-%EC%9B%90%EB%8B%A8-%ED%85%8D%EC%8A%A4%EC%B2%98-%EC%83%89%EC%83%81-%EC%A0%9C%EA%B1%B0) | Remove the color while maintaining the pattern or texture of the texture image and change it to another color. **Repeat** | **Repeat** | Repeat the image. **Space /** **Shift** | Adjust the space and shift value between repeated textures. **Extend to Other Side** | If the image intersects with the grid, extend it to the other side. **Transformation** | **Pivot** | Set the Pivot position of the image. **Position** | Move the image based on the Position of the Pivot. **Size/Angle** | Set the size and angle of the image. **Flip** | ## ![20252.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53053863372569) Flip an image either horizontally or vertically within the Texture Editor. **Reset** | Click the Reset button for the Position, Size and Angle properties to revert back to the original image. #### **Preview Settings** 1. Click the ![image__2_.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360090976493) **Preview Settings** in the upper right corner of the Texture Editor. → The Preview Settings window appears. 2. Set the options below. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Show Grid** | View or hide the grid. **Occlude Opacity** | Set the Opacity of repeated images in the Preview window. #### **Apply Texture** 1. When the texture editing is complete, click the **Apply & Close** button at the bottom right of the Texture Editor. → The edited texture is applied. #### **Save Texture Image** ![Youtube Icon.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44161782043801)[ Watch Video](https://youtu.be/kOsqnvb583Q?feature=shared&t=168) 1. Click **OK** to select a folder in which to save the selected images. title: Edit Notch Properties
content: 1. Select the notch using the ![Notch On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/48650245208217)**Notch** tool in the 2D toolbar. 2. Set notch properties as needed. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Name** | Change the name for the notch. **Type** | Select the notch shape. **T** | ![tshape.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024213047) **V** | ![vshape.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024296288) **I** | ![ishape.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024213067) **L** | ![__.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360059145773) **U** | ![ushape.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024296248) **Box** | ![boxshape.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024213087) **Angle** | **Perpendicular** | Notch is placed perpendicular to the line. **Custom** | Arbitrarily decide in what angle the notch is created based on the line. **Length** | Edit notch length as needed. This option appears or disappears according to the notch setting under [Settings ▶ User Settings ▶ 2D](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360001558747). The notches export in the configured size. **Direction** | Decide in which direction the notch is created. This option is activated only when the notch is created at a corner. **Point (Center)** | Notch is created at the center of two lines making the corner. **Segment 1** | Notch is shifted towards a line. **Segment 2** | Notch is shifted towards the other line. **Notch Placement** | ![Label.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/48650245208857) Decide where the notch is located on the Seam Allowance. [![Youtube Icon.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/50833157563673)](https://youtu.be/sh739ZhJQHw?si=Yr87n9ldy-bJIMiH) **Point (Center)** | Notch is located at the center. **Seamline Extension** | Notch is located and extended from the pattern outline. **Point Perpendicular** | Notch is located and perpendicular to the segment point. **📝Note:** Available only in combination with Direction in Point (Center). **Seam Allowance Perpendicular** | Notch is located and perpendicular to seam allowance. **📝Note:** Available only in combination with Direction in Point (Center). **Flip** | Flip the notch to the other side of the line. **Lock** | Fix the notch position when moving the point of the pattern outline to where the notch was created. **Lock Position** | When setting the notch's fixed position, select the position of the reference point. **Start/End Point** | Set the position to fix the notch. **Grading Size** **(**[**![Youtube Icon.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/26243410803481)Watch Video**](https://youtu.be/CwB8_ad328M?si=FG3gZ82C3FAw-ayR&t=2109)**)** | **Fixed** | Instead of moving the notches proportionally with the grading size, it fixes them in a specific position. You can do the same when importing [DXF](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000493067-2D-Pattern-DXF-Import-Export) files. _**✨Tip:**_ Default notch shape and length can be set in [Settings ▶ User Settings ▶ 2D](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360001558747).
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on using the Notch tool in the 2D toolbar of CLO 3D, detailing how to select and customize notch properties for precise pattern design.

title: Rotate Dart
content: Move a dart to a new location or divide it by rotating it. **Please note that this option only appears if both sides of the dart are the exact same length.** **Rotate to a New Location** 1. Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit**▶ Edit Pattern** 2D Toolbar **▶![Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Edit.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/36791106874009) Edit Pattern** 2. Right-click after selecting both segments of a dart. → A right-click pop-up menu appears. 3. Select **Rotate Dart** and click on the pattern outline to draw a new dart location. → The centerline of the original dart appears as a guideline. 4. Click on the guideline to set a pivot point. → The pattern is divided into two parts. 5. Click and move the mouse towards the direction where the selected part should rotate. → The dart is rotated to the selected location. 6. Move the mouse cursor along the new dart's centerline to set its length. → The dart is completely rotated with the new length. **Rotate into Another Dart** 1. Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit**▶ Edit Pattern** 2D Toolbar **▶![Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Edit.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/36791106874009) Edit Pattern** 2. Right-click after selecting both segments of a dart. → A right-click pop-up menu appears. 3. Select **Rotate Dart** and click another dart's intersection. → Both segments of the dart are automatically selected. → The pattern is divided into two at the intersection of two darts' centerlines. 4. Click and move the mouse towards the direction where the selected pattern should rotate. → The dart is rotated to the selected location. 5. Move the mouse cursor along the new dart's centerline to set its length. → The dart is completely rotated with the new length. **📝****Note:** * Right-click while rotating or setting the length to input specific values. * When rotating darts, a baseline is automatically generated on the rotated dart.
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for rotating and repositioning darts in a 2D pattern, ensuring precise modifications while adhering to length requirements.

If the CLO software is not Standalone Onlineauth, please go to the download page after signing in and install the right version. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/52747524784537) 4. If the PC's 443 port firewall is blocked, unblock and try logging in again. 5. Deactivate the antivirus program on the PC and try logging in again. 6. If the above steps do not solve your problem, please reach out via [Contact Us](http://clo3d.com/contact). **CLO for Business Users** **Standalone** 1. Check the [HASP Driver](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000615488#Click3) is properly installed, and try logging in again. 3. Confirm internet connection. 4. title: CLO to MetaHuman: USD Garment Integration Workflow
content:
This guide outlines the entire workflow for exporting garments from Marvelous Designer as USD and integrating them with Unreal Engine **MetaHuman**. * * * ### **⭐1. Project Initialization and Plugin Setup** #### **1-1: Installing Core Data** Ensure you have **Unreal Engine 5.6** or later installed before proceeding. 1. Open the **Epic Games Launcher** and navigate to the **Library** tab. 2. Locate your Unreal Engine installation card. 3. Click the **down arrow** next to the **Launch** button and select **Options**. 4. In the installation options window, check the box next to **MetaHuman Creator Core Data**. 5. Click **Apply** to download and install the required data. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53323164145945) #### **1-2: Project Configuration** 1. Create or open your Unreal Engine project. 2. Navigate to **Edit > Project Settings** in the main menu. 3. In the left sidebar, scroll down to the **Plugins** section and select **MetaHuman SDK**. 4. Locate the setting labeled **MetaHuman Packaging Paths**. > **⚠️ Warning:** **Do not change the name of this folder path.** Due to a known issue, the workaround currently in place relies on this folder retaining its default name. Modifying it will break the packaging process. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53323158561817) #### **1-3: Outfits Directory Setup** By default, the location for Outfits is `/Game/Outfits`. In your **Content Browser** , this path appears as **All > Content > Outfits**. You should create and edit all your Outfit Assets within this directory. **Important for FAB Uploads:** If you plan to use the **MetaHuman Manager** to verify and package your asset for FAB, you must adhere to a strict folder structure: * Your Outfit Asset and **all of its dependencies** must reside in a single subfolder within the `/Game/Outfits` directory. * If assets are scattered outside this specific subfolder, the MetaHuman Manager will fail the verification process, and packaging will be impossible. #### **1-4: Plugin Setup** Make sure to enable **Chaos Cloth Plugins** and **MetaHuman Creator Plugin** , and restart your Unreal Engine project. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53323164146329) ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53323164146585) * * * ### **⭐2: Preparing MetaHumans for Export (UE 5.6 and later)** #### **2-1: Create and Customize the MetaHuman** 1. In the **Content Browser** , right-click and navigate to **MetaHuman > MetaHuman Character**. 2. Open the newly created MetaHuman asset to enter the editor. 3. Customize the character’s attributes (Face and Body Measurements) as needed. #### **2-2: Configure Assembly Settings** Once customization is complete, prepare the asset for export: 1. Navigate to the **Assembly** tab. 2. Select **Download Textures**. 3. Check the box for **Create Full Rig**. 4. Change the Assembly Target from **UE Cine (Complete)** to **(DCC Export)**. 5. Select your desired **Output Folder**. 6. Click the **Assembly** button to generate the files. > **ℹ️ Integration Note:** Successfully completing this step saves the specific Body and Head files required for **DNA Import in CLO**. You will need this DNA file in the next section to accurately fit garments to your MetaHuman body. * * * ### ⭐**3: Import MetaHuman DNA into CLO (CLO 2025.2 or later)** 1. Launch **CLO**. 2. Navigate to **File > Import > DNA** in the main menu. 3. Browse to the output folder you defined in the previous section. 4. Select the exported **Body** and **Head** files. 5. Click **OK** to complete the import. For more details, please refer to the following CLO manual for more details: [**MetaHuman DNA Importer**](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/51821648831257-MetaHuman-DNA-Importer) * * * ### **⭐4: Prepare Garment in CLO and Bake UV Maps** #### **4-1: Garment Simulation** 1. Create a new garment or apply existing garments. 2. Run the Simulation to drape and fit the garments onto the imported MetaHuman body. #### **4-2: UV Preparation** Before exporting, ensure the UV maps are correctly packed to prevent texture issues. 1. Switch the view to the **UV Editor**. 2. Select the **whole garment** (all patterns). 3. Run **UV Packing** to organize the UV islands efficiently. #### **4-3: Exporting to USD files** 1. Navigate to **File > Export > USD**. 2. In the export dialog window, configure the settings exactly as follows: **Setting Category** | **Configuration** ---|--- **Object** | Select **Include Garment** **Patterns** | Choose **Select All Patterns** **Geometry** | Set to **Single Object** **Thickness** | Select **Thick** **Textures** | Check**Unified UV Coordinates** and **Select All Maps** **Simulation** | Check **Include Garment Simulation Data** * * * ### **⭐5: Convert Style into a Resizable MetaHuman Wardrobe Asset** #### **5-1: Prepare Project and Import USD Outfit** **Step 1: Open Your Project** Launch Unreal Engine 5.6 (or later) and open your target project. **Step 2: Establish Directory Structure** You must establish a precise folder hierarchy in the **Content Browser**. This structure is critical for asset validation. 1. Navigate to `/Game/Outfits/`. 2. Create a folder named after your asset (e.g., `Style01`). 3. **Crucial Step:** Inside that folder, create a **subfolder with the exact same name** (`Style01`). Your hierarchy should look like this:
```
Content
└── Outfits ├── Meshes <-- Store MetaHuman (MH) skeletal files here └── Style01 <-- Main Asset Folder └── Style01 <-- Working Folder (Import USDs here)
``` **Folder Purpose Definitions:** * **Meshes:** Dedicated storage for MetaHuman skeletal and mesh files. * **Main Folder (e.g., Style01):** This parent folder will eventually contain _only_ the finalized wardrobe asset. * **Working Folder (e.g., Style01/Style01):** This is your workspace. All development, importing, and editing must take place here. You may organize subfolders inside this directory as needed. **Step 3: Export the MetaHuman Reference Mesh** You need the skeletal mesh from your MetaHuman to serve as a reference. 1. Navigate to your MetaHuman asset location. 2. Locate the **Skeletal Mesh** for the body (not the Blueprint). 3. Right-click the asset and select **Asset Actions > Export**. 4. Save this file to the `Outfits/Meshes` folder you created in Step 2. **Step 4: Import the USD Outfit** 1. Navigate to your working folder: `Outfits > Style01 > Style01`. 2. Import your USD outfit file into this folder. 3. In the **USD Import Options** dialog, leave all settings at their **Default** values and click **Import**. Unreal Engine will automatically generate subfolders for _Textures_ , _Materials_ , and _Static Meshes_. Locate and double-click the **Static Mesh** of the outfit to open it. **🔧 Troubleshooting: Transparency Issues** If your garment appears transparent or ghostly in the viewport, follow these steps to fix the material blend mode: 1. In the details panel or content browser, find the material applied to the mesh. 2. Right-click the material instance and select **Find Parent**. 3. Open the Parent Material. 4. Scroll down to the **Material Property Overrides** section. 5. Locate **Blend Mode**. 6. Change the dropdown from **Translucent** to **Opaque**. 7. **Save** and **Apply** the material. #### **5-2: Create and Configure Cloth Asset** **Step 1: Create the Cloth Asset** First, you need to generate the base asset files in your project directory. 1. Navigate to your **Working folder**. 2. **Right-click** > **Physics** > **Cloth Asset**. 3. Name the asset clearly (e.g., `CA_Style01`). > **Note:** This automatically creates a **DataFlow node** with a "DF" prefix. This node is required for the asset to function—do not delete or modify it. **Step 2: Open and Clean the Dataflow Graph** Set up the workspace by removing unnecessary simulation nodes. 1. **Right-click** on your new CA Node (`CA_Style01`). 2. Select **Open in Dataflow Editor (Experimental)**. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53335888520729) 3. **Clean up the graph:** Since you are not running a simulation, delete all nodes **EXCEPT** the following: * `Transfer Skin Weights` * `Remesh` * `ClothAssetTerminal` * _(Optional)_ You may also delete the purple and brown explanatory notes. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53335876830233) **Step 3: Import and Connect Static Mesh** Now, import your specific outfit geometry and establish the node connections. 1. **Add Import Node:** Right-click in the graph, type **StaticMeshImport** , and select it. 2. **Configure Node Details** (Bottom-right panel): * **Uncheck:** `Import Sim Mesh` (as you do not have one). * **Static Mesh:** Drag in or select your outfit mesh (e.g., `style01`). 3. **Connect the Nodes:** * Drag from `StaticMeshImport` (**Collection**) → `TransferSkinWeights` (**Collection**). * Drag from `TransferSkinWeights` (**Collection**) → `Remesh` (**Collection**). * Drag from `TransferSkinWeights` (**Collection**) → `ClothAssetTerminal`. * Drag from `Remesh` (**Collection**) → `Collection Lods 1` (on the Terminal node). **Step 4: Configure Skin Weights** Adjust the `TransferSkinWeights` node to map the outfit to the character body correctly. 1. Click on the **TransferSkinWeights** node. 2. Update the **Node Details** panel with the following settings: * **Target Mesh(es):** Change to `Render Mesh`. * **Render Mesh Transfer Source:** Change to `Skeletal Mesh`. * **Transfer Method:** Change to `Closest Point on Surface`. * **Source Asset:** Drag in or select the combined body mesh paired with the garment (e.g., `Character01_CombinedSkelMesh`). **Step 5: Visualize the Asset** Verify your work in the Construction Viewport. 1. Click on the **Remesh** node in the graph. 2. Locate the **Construction Viewport** (the window to the _left_ of the Simulation Viewport). 3. If the viewport is empty: * Click the **View Mode Dropdown** (Top right of the viewport, icon looks like a cube). * Select **Render**. 4. Save Project. #### **5-3: Create and Configure Wardrobe Asset for MetaHuman Creator** **📂Step 1: Organize Folders** Before starting, ensure your file structure is clean to avoid referencing errors. 1. Navigate to your main folder → **Style01**. 2. Ensure this folder contains **only** your **Working folder** (which should be named identically to your intended outfit asset or use the `OA_` prefix). 3. Remove any other loose assets or extraneous folders. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53335845173657) **👕Step 2: Create the Outfit Asset** Generate the core asset file using the physics menu. 1. **Right-click** in the folder → **Physics** → **Outfit Asset**. 2. **Name the Asset:** * Must match your folder name exactly. * _Recommended Format:_ `OA_Style01`. 3. **Select Template:** * Choose **Resizable Outfit** when prompted. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53335817349529) **📦Step 3: Manage the Dataflow (DF) Node** A dependency node is automatically created and must be stored correctly. 1. Locate the new node prefixed with `DF_`. 2. Drag it into your **Working folder**. 3. Select **Move Here**. > **Note:** This step is required for packaging in Fab and ensuring compatibility with the MetaHuman Manager. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53335849553433) **⚙️Step 4: Configure the Dataflow Editor** Open the editor and optimize performance settings before adding heavy assets. 1. **Double-click** your new Outfit Asset (`OA_Style01`) to open the Dataflow Editor. 2. Locate the **Evaluate Dataflow Graph** button in the top toolbar. 3. Click the **three dots** next to it. 4. Select **Manual Graph Evaluation**. * _Why?_ This prevents the engine from trying to process changes after every single click, avoiding long wait times during setup. **🧵Step 5: Add Cloth Assets** Link your Cloth Assets (CA) and Skeletal Meshes to the Outfit Asset. 1. **Dataflow Members Panel** (Bottom Left): * Check the box for **Sized Outfit Source**. * Click the **Plus (+)** sign for each cloth asset you need to add. 2. **Configure Each Entry:** * **Source Asset:** Select your cloth asset (e.g., `CA_Style01`). * **Size Name:** Enter a descriptive name. * **SourceBodyParts:** Add your combined skeletal mesh (e.g., `Character01_combinedSkelMesh`). * **Num Resizing Interpolation Points:** * _Default:_ 1500 * _Recommended Range:_ 1000–2500 * _Tip:_ Higher numbers are more accurate but process slower. 3. **Variable Overrides:** * Switch to the **Dataflow Tab** (Bottom Left). * Find **Variable Overrides** and check the box for **SIZE OUTFIT SOURCE**. * Verify that both the `CA_` asset and the `CombinedSkelMesh` are successfully linked. **⏳Step 6: Evaluate the Graph** Process the data to generate the outfit sizes. 1. Click **Evaluate Dataflow Graph** in the top toolbar. 2. **Wait:** Watch the progress bar as it processes each size. This may take several minutes. 3. **Reset:** Once complete, click the three-dot menu again and turn **Automatic Evaluation** back on. **🔄Step 7: Re-Evaluation (Troubleshooting)** If you modify any input assets later (cloth, static mesh, etc.), you must force a re-evaluation. 1. Click **Evaluate Dataflow Graph**. 2. **If no progress bar appears:** * Right-click the **Sized Outfit Source** node → **Evaluate**. * _OR_ Right-click the **OutfitAssetTerminal** node → **Evaluate**. **💾Step 8: Save** * **Save your Outfit Asset** to preserve all configurations. **👤Step 9: Test in MetaHuman Creator (MHC)** Verify the outfit works on a character and resizes correctly. 1. **Create Test Character:** * Content Browser → Right-click → **MetaHuman** → **MetaHuman Character**. * Name the character. 2. **Open in MHC:** * Open the character and navigate to the **Hair & Clothing** tab. * Scroll to **Outfit Clothing**. 3. **Apply Outfit:** * Remove the current **Wardrobe Asset**. * Drag your **Outfit Asset** (`OA_Style01`) into this slot. * Double-click to apply. 4. **Test Resizing:** * Use body sliders or apply different presets to ensure the clothing adapts to the body shape. **🧥Step 10: Verify Wardrobe Item** * After applying the outfit, check your Content Browser. * A new asset should appear: `WI_Style01` (Wardrobe Item). * * * ### **⭐6. MetaHuman Outfit Testing Checklist** The following checklist provides quality assurance for the MetaHuman testing phase. Use this to systematically verify that your `OA_` asset resizes correctly without breaking. **1\. Preparation** * [ ] **Clean State:** Ensure the character has no other clothing layers underneath that might cause false clipping positives. * [ ] **Asset Applied:** Verify `OA_Style01` is successfully slotted in the **Outfit Clothing** section. * [ ] **Visibility:** Zoom in close to the garment boundaries (necklines, cuffs, waistbands). **2\. The "Extremes" (Stress Testing)** _This is where most resizing errors occur. If it works here, it usually works everywhere._ * [ ] **Maximum Bulk:** Set sliders/preset to **Tall + Heavy/Overweight**. * _Check for:_ Skin poking through the cloth (clipping) at the stomach, shoulders, and thighs. * [ ] **Minimum Frame:** Set sliders/preset to **Short + Thin/Underweight**. * _Check for:_ "Floating" geometry where the cloth is too far from the skin, or collapsing geometry where the mesh overlaps itself. **3\. Specific Body Regions** _Adjust individual sliders if your interface allows, or select specific presets._ * [ ] **Chest/Bust:** Maximize and minimize. Check for texture stretching or distortion on logos/patterns. * [ ] **Shoulders:** Widen and narrow. Check if straps (if applicable) stay aligned or slide off. * [ ] **Waist/Hips:** Check the transition area. If this is a shirt, ensure it doesn't clip into the pants line (or vice versa). **4\. Visual Inspection Criteria** * [ ] **Clipping:** No skin showing through the fabric. * [ ] **Distortion:** No extreme stretching of the UVs/texture (e.g., plaid patterns looking like spaghetti). * [ ] **Seams:** Ensure the vertices at the seams are not splitting apart during resizing. * [ ] **Neckline:** Ensure the collar doesn't eat into the neck on "Heavy" settings. **5\. Final Verification** * [ ] **Reset to Neutral:** Return to **Average Height + Average Weight**. Does the mesh snap back perfectly? * [ ] **Asset Generation:** Confirm that the `WI_Style01` (Wardrobe Item) exists in the content browser after your tests.
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for exporting garments from Marvelous Designer as USD files and seamlessly integrating them with Unreal Engine's MetaHuman framework.

title: Modes
content: There are three available modes in the upper right dropdown menu of the CLO window: **Simulation** , **Print Layout** , and **Emulator**. **** In **Simulation** mode**,** it is possible to create and edit patterns in the 2D window, and in the 3D window drape garments, edit poses, or perform various other actions. **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115000306927/_____.png)** In**Print Layout** mode, you can manually place patterns on prints to match texture placements, calculate fabric consumption, and create printable pattern layouts. **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115000306987/_______.png)** In**Emulator** mode, you can enter the values of fabrics created with the CLO Fabric Kit (the precursor of the new CLO zFab Kit.) **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115000303148/_____.png)**
content_description: Explore the three versatile modes of the CLO window—Simulation, Print Layout, and Emulator—each designed to enhance your pattern creation, garment draping, and fabric management experience.

title: Rectangle
content: **Objective** Create rectangle Patterns in 2D window. **Location** Main Menu ▶ 2D ▶ Create ▶ **Rectangle** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![Rectangle.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53143504333977) **Rectangle** **Operation** 1.
